# Chasm fall recordings

- `male-falling-scream.mp3`: **man scream**, by **alexaxy**, https://freesound.org/people/alexaxy/sounds/278177/ ? CC0 1.0. Preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/278/278177_3207011-hq.mp3
- `river-body-splash.mp3`: **jump-into-water.flac**, by **yurkobb**, https://freesound.org/people/yurkobb/sounds/280219/ ? CC0 1.0. Preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/280/280219_2023784-hq.mp3
- Both are real recordings. The scream starts at offset 0.8 seconds and fades over 3 seconds; the water impact starts 3 seconds after release. No generated vocal tones.


# Bat ambience

- `bats-colony-loop.wav`: **Hundreds of bats screaming and coming out of their nest**, by **felix.blume** (Felix Blume).
- Source: https://freesound.org/people/felix.blume/sounds/245768/
- Preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/245/245768_1661766-lq.mp3
- License: **CC0 1.0**.
- Real bat field recording from Argens-Minervois, France. Excerpt 00:30?00:42, mono 22050 Hz PCM with 30 ms edge fades for looping.

# Scene 2 Gregorian background music

- Preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/780/780488_264532-hq.mp3

# Halo neck trap vocal

- `male-choked-cry.mp3`: **Male Choking_2**, by **Drkvixn91**, https://freesound.org/people/Drkvixn91/sounds/317440/ ? **CC0 1.0**.
- Preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/317/317440_5057106-hq.mp3
- Recorded male performance of choking and struggling to breathe. Plays once when the halo traps the neck, with normalized volume, leading silence removed and a fade out within 4.35 seconds. Stops if Lucia is destroyed or the scene ends.


# Scene 2 replacement: vocals only

- `gregorian-vocals.mp3`: **A cappella - Gregorian lamento**, by **Vrymaa**, https://freesound.org/people/Vrymaa/sounds/738774/ ? **CC BY 4.0**, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.
- Male tenor/countertenor vocal performance, no instruments. Author describes the recording as clean and without background noise.
- Adaptation: opening 45-second choir excerpt, 0.75-second loop crossfade, 70 Hz high-pass and 7 kHz low-pass filters, low playback volume. Attribution also appears in the initial instructions. Replaces the previous choir-and-organ field recording.


# Scene 2: traditional Gregorian chant, female vocal

- `salve-regina-female.m4a`: **Salve Regina, simple tone**, performed and published by **Veronica Brandt**, linked in the recordings section of https://littleoffice.brandt.id.au/.
- License stated by the project: **CC BY 4.0**, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Attribution appears in the opening instructions.
- Recording: https://d3ctxlq1ktw2nl.cloudfront.net/staging/2021-08-10/dc0c75ef10c29f5a385335e573dddd25.m4a
- Full recording at original pitch and speed, 0.25-second crossfade at the loop seam and gentle 70 Hz / 7 kHz filters. Replaces the Gregorian-style improvisation by Vrymaa.


# Active scene 2 music: male Gregorian church choir

- `gregorian-male-ave-maria.ogg`: **Ave Maria** from Gregorian Vespers for Saint Vincent Pallotti, performed by **Schola Gregoriana**, Pallottine Seminary in O?tarzew, Poland, conducted by **Dariusz Smolarek**, June 8, 2007.
- Source and permission: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Schola_Gregoriana-Ave_Maria.ogg
- Original: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/23/Schola_Gregoriana-Ave_Maria.ogg
- License: **CC BY-SA 3.0**, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. The original recording is included unchanged; the playback adaptation (0.25-second loop crossfade and gentle 70 Hz / 7 kHz filters) is offered under the same license. Attribution is included in the opening instructions.
- Male liturgical choir, original pitch and speed. Replaces the female Salve Regina recording in scene 2.

# Scene 3: real wolf howl before the werewolf appears

- `wolf-howls.ogg`: **Wolf howls**, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
- Source and public-domain statement: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Wolf_howls.ogg
- Original: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/87/Wolf_howls.ogg
- Public domain (U.S. federal government recording). Original file included unchanged.
- Playback: 13.35?17.55 seconds, original pitch and speed, 0.06-second fade in and 0.25-second fade out. Replaces the synthesized howl. The werewolf appears after playback ends.


# Active scene 3 howl: one real husky, one isolated call

- `solo-husky-howl.mp3`: **dog howling.wav**, recorded by **simcotter**.
- Source: https://freesound.org/people/simcotter/sounds/115357/
- License: **CC0 1.0**, https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/.
- High-quality preview: https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/115/115357_2024015-hq.mp3
- Author describes a husky dog recorded with a hard disk recorder. This replaces the wolf-pack recording above.
- Playback: one isolated howl, 9.10?11.35 seconds, original pitch and speed, 0.06-second fade in and 0.25-second fade out. No layering, looping or added echoes. The werewolf appears after the isolated call ends.
